confirmed: Initial successful real 12-second AAC transcode: upstream sends initial stream_progress, stream_open with isTranscodeComplete false, and explicit stream_closed to each of two owner sockets; unrelated-user socket receives none. Go emits none. Both serve playlist200, nonempty segment200, and finish real FFmpeg output.

Active 240-second transcode: upstream sends incremental percent/chunks/numSegments and stream_open once per owner socket; Go emits none. Both streams remain active at25s, then close200 removes directory and HLS becomes404. This is incremental-progress/active-close evidence, not long successful completion.

Fast completed restart from saved120s to missing segment0: upstream emits delayed initial stream_progress then stream_ready to both owner sockets. Go emits none. Both missing-segment requests404 and close200 removes directory/HLS404. Segment-zero restart correctly emits no stream_reset because upstream tests the returned zero value.

Corrupt real AAC input: upstream attempts copy, retries AAC after10s cancellation wait, then emits stream_error with id and nonempty error to both owner sockets, removes directory and detaches HLS404. Go logs FFmpeg error but emits no error, retains directory/HLS200 until explicit close. Neither persisted a playback session or media progress for this unlistened session.

Executable /usr/bin/false configured as FFmpeg: upstream capability/start preparation failure triggers AAC retry then stream_error to owner sockets without initial progress; directory removed/HLS404. Go returns session200 then retains directory/HLS200 without error. This is a failing executable/preparation scenario, not proof of ENOENT spawn behavior.

All six distinct live variants preserve explicit close response200 OK and final directory removal/HLS404. Two-owner delivery is per socket, not duplicate emission to a single recipient. No lifecycle traffic reached the unrelated user.
